sources.citation: Грум-Гржимайло, Г. Е. 1899. Описание путешествия в Западный Китай, т. II. СПб.: Имп. Русское географическое общество. Приложение VI «Список слов наречия тангутов панака», с. 417-420 (PDF pp. 483-486).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: A bare Russian-Cyrillic wordlist of c. 330 items recorded through a Dungan interpreter; no stress marks on any form and no remark on stress or pronunciation beyond quoting Rockhill. This is the wordlist Kara 1984 re-edited and the sole Panang-specific primary data.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (J. Green, SIL East Asia). 2012. Change Request 2012-029: merge [pcr] Panang into [adx] Amdo Tibetan (adopted 2013-01-23). 6 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that 'Panang' (Tibetan sbra.nag 'black tent') is a subgroup of Amdo Tibetans; Denwood 1999:30 and the data in Kara 1984 show it is 'nothing more than a variety of Amdo Tibetan'.

sources.citation: Грум-Гржимайло, Г. Е. 1896 (т. I), 1907 (т. III: Вокруг Куку-нора..), and 1903 Материалы по этнологии Амдо и области Куку-нора (Изв. ИРГО 39/5). scanned texts.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent словарь/ударение/панака: vol. III has ethnographic chapters on the Panaka (Kokonor Tangut) nomads; no linguistic description, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Rockhill, W. W. 1891. The Land of the Lamas: notes of a journey through China, Mongolia and Tibet. New York: Century. Appendix VII 'Notes on the language of Eastern Tibet', pp. 361 ff. (Panak'a of the Koko-nor).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only pronunciation remarks (Koko-nor pronunciation 'harsher than that in any other section'; syllabary comparing Lhasa, Bat'ang, Ts'arong); no statement about stress or accent. Preface says some vowels in transcription are accented but 'pronounced as in French', i.e. diacritics mark vowel quality, not stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page pana1292 (Panang, bookkeeping) and hh.bib listing for [adx] Amdo Tibetan (28 grammar/phonology/sketch entries).
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive reference for pana1292 apart from the ISO change request; all descriptive literature (Sun 1986, Haller 2004, Ebihara 2011/2019, Caplow 2009, Wang 2022, etc.) is filed under Amdo Tibetan amdo1237.

sources.citation: Ebihara, Shiho. 2011. Amdo Tibetan. In Yasuhiro Yamakoshi (ed.), Grammatical sketches from the field, 41-78. Tokyo: ILCAA, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

sources.note: Concise English sketch (Gonghe / Chabcha, Qinghai) with a phonology section

sources.citation: Wang, Shuangcheng. 2022. Study of the Phonology of Amdo Tibetan Dialects. Leiden: Brill. 306 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, paywalled at the publisher (DOI); library e-access not checked
sources.note: Recent dialect-comparative phonology of Amdo covering pastoral (nomad) and farming varieties; would state whether stress is fixed in nomad dialects around Qinghai Lake.

sources.citation: Caplow, Nancy J. 2009. The role of stress in Tibetan tonogenesis: a study in historical comparative acoustics. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 607 pp. (and Caplow 2016, Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 39(2): 'Stress patterns and acoustic correlates of stress in Balti Tibetan' / Rebkong Amdo data).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: The only instrumental study of Tibetan word stress that includes Rebkong Amdo; would supply an acoustically grounded stress statement for Amdo.

sources.citation: Haller, Felix. 2004. Dialekt und Erzählungen von Themchen: sprachwissenschaftliche Beschreibung eines Nomadendialektes aus Nord-Amdo (Beiträge zur tibetischen Erzählforschung 14). Bonn: VGH Wissenschaftsverlag. 442 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number PL1621.T54 H35 2004x)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number PL1621.T54 H35 2004x
sources.note: The fullest description of a North-Amdo nomad (black-tent) dialect from the Qinghai Lake region, i.e. the same sbra-nag population Panang denotes; its phonology chapter is the closest place a Panang-type stress statement would live. Filed under amdo1237 in Glottolog.

sources.citation: Sun, Jackson T.-S. 1986. Aspects of the phonology of Amdo Tibetan: Ndzorge Śæme Xɤra dialect (Monumenta Serindica 16). Tokyo: ILCAA. vii+267 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Standard phonological monograph on a nomad Amdo dialect; treats suprasegmentals and is the usual citation for Amdo stress/absence of tone. Supersedes anything Panang-specific.

sources.citation: Kara, György. 1984. A Sbra-nag glossary in Grum-Gržimajlo's Travels. In L. Ligeti (ed.), Tibetan and Buddhist Studies commemorating the 200th anniversary of the birth of Alexander Csoma de Kőrös, vol. 1, 321-362. Budapest: Akadémiai Kiadó.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only work Glottolog/ISO cite for Panang; a philological re-edition of the 1899 wordlist with Written-Tibetan identifications. Wordlist type, so unlikely to state a stress rule, but it is the the deciding source for the retired code.

sources.citation: Denwood, Philip. 1999. Tibetan (London Oriental and African Language Library 3). Amsterdam: Benjamins, p. 30.
